content:
nitya: noticing recurring short latency stutters (30-200ms) for long-context decodes (~30-60k tokens) on several prod hosts this morning. p95/p99 jumps align with KV evict bursts.
omar: can you dump a small profiler sample and the eviction log?
nitya: pasted quick snippet from host-12: ```[2026-02-14T09:12:03Z] kv_evict: policy=fifo, evicted=3584, reclaim_ms=22, inflight_reinsert=8
[2026-02-14T09:12:03Z] decode: req_id=xx, latency=410ms, baseline=120ms
stack: runtime::kv::evict -> runtime::gpu::copy -> runtime::batcher::dispatch```
elaine: we shipped the reinsert-on-hit change in the small-key path last month, maybe that's interacting with FIFO under high concurrency
kai: I saw a similar blip in canary last Friday but dismissed as noise. can we repro with a synthetic workload?
omar: easiest repro is long-context replay + bursty decode batcher toggles. I'll try a 64-concurrent decode with context=40k.
perf-bot: perf test queued: jobs/kv-stutter-177777 (ETA ~8m)
nitya: note: allocation churn spikes when evict+reinsert happen simultaneously, looks like short-lived double allocation -> paging -> stutter
elain: typo: that's "elaine" — but yes, allocator profiles would help. do we have flamegraph for the reclaim path?
omar: attaching flame fragment (summarized): ```kv::evict 40%
allocator::alloc 25%
copy_to_gpu 20%
batcher::drain 10%```
kai: that ordering indicates eviction+alloc pressure is in the critical path for serving threads, not background GC
elaine: theory: FIFO favors older entries and when combined with immediate reinserts (on hits) we create churn where the same kv blocks oscillate between in-cache and evicted states during a bursted access pattern
omar: also saw LRU indicator counters rising right before each spike — suggests policy mixing is toggling heuristics under pressure
nitya: what's the temporal pattern? are spikes aligned with batcher window size changes?
omar: yes — when batcher moves from size 4->16 (burst), eviction rate briefly triples for ~50-200ms windows
itya: @omar can you try disabling reinserts for in-flight requests in a canary?
omar: on it. deploying patch patch/kv-defer-reinsert to canary-2 now.
deploy-bot: deploy started patch/kv-defer-reinsert -> canary-2 (id: d-2026-02-14-0918)
perf-bot: canary run started: kv-stutter-177777-canary
itya: also want to try making evict prefer cold partitions (partition-protection) during high inflight. might be low-hanging fix
kai: agree. we have partition tags per-request metadata, we can bias evict score by recent_reuse_count
omar: quick canary results: with reinserts deferred p99 drops from 420ms -> 150ms during the burst windows. baseline unchanged.
itya: good signal. any regressions on memory?
omar: memory stable, eviction counts slightly higher but no paging thrash
itya: next steps: 1) open a small RFC for deferring reinserts + inflight protection, 2) run wider canary on dedicated pool, 3) add allocator metrics to kv evict logs.
elain: I'll own the RFC and PR. assigning follow-ups in ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RI-1289
kai: add test that simulates batcher-size oscillation to CI perf harness
itya: thanks all — sounds like we have a plausible root cause (evict+reinsert churn + FIFO/LRU hybrid toggling under bursty batcher) and a low-risk mitigation. will monitor post-deploy. :thumbsup:
